newsitem.title: MOLDOVA: Challenger leads but Moldovan election tight.
newsitem.headline: Challenger leads but Moldovan election tight.

text.p: Left-wing challenger Petru Lucinschi had a lead of just one point over President Mircea Snegur as counting in Moldova's presidential election run-off passed the halfway stage on Monday, electoral officials said.
The race, which followed a bitter campaign, had tightened considerably since the first results were announced.

Lucinschi, chairman of the national parliament, had 50.5 percent of the vote after 55 percent of Sunday's ballot had been counted. Snegur, who has been president since independence in 1991, had 49.5 percent.

No figures were yet available for the capital Chisinau, where 750,000 of the 4.3 million Moldovans live. Lucinschi is expected to do well among the former Soviet republic's large and mainly urban Russian-speaking minority.
Votes are counted by hand in the 2,000 or so polling stations nationwide and the results are then centralised at district and national level.
Electoral officials declined to explain why results from Chisinau were not yet available but said there had been a similar delay in the first round of voting on November 17.
